## Summary

Ensure the herdr audit-freshness predicate enforces the canonical "at-or-near"
semantics and is the **single source of truth** shared by both the icon display
and the downtime (audit-dispatch) worker.

Audit freshness currently lives only in `isAuditFresh()` in
`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`. It is the basis for the icon display
(`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) AND is the documented freshness gate reused by the
downtime dispatch audit tier (`selectAuditCandidate` /
`getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, which
treats `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` as "needs a fresh `/skill:audit`").

Running an audit itself bumps the work item's `updatedAt` to within a fraction
of a second of its `auditedAt` (`wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` +
the verdict-driven status transition). A freshness rule that requires a strict
gap on one side (e.g. only `auditedAt` comfortably ahead of `updatedAt`) can
therefore disagree with the just-persisted state. The canonical fix in
SorraAgents (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4) treats an audit as fresh when its
`auditedAt` is **at or near** the item's `updatedAt` (within a small
tolerance) because a near-simultaneous `updatedAt` bump is the audit's own
persistence write.

This item makes ContextHub's herdr audit-freshness logic follow the same
at-or-near rule so the icon display and the downtime dispatcher agree, and
never disagree on a just-persisted audit.

## Expected behaviour

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true (fresh) when `auditedAt`
  is at-or-near `updatedAt` within a small, named tolerance (the audit's own
  persistence write), and false otherwise.
- The icon (`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) shows the fresh icon for a
  just-persisted audit (no longer shows the stale glyph for an audit the run
  just persisted).
- The downtime audit candidate selection (`selectAuditCandidate` /
  `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`) uses the SAME
  `isAuditFresh` predicate, so a just-persisted fresh audit is NOT a dispatch
  candidate (no redundant `/skill:audit` re-run).
- Only one freshness definition exists; neither consumer re-implements its
  own comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditFresh` in `icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` at-or-near `updatedAt`
   (within a documented tolerance constant) as fresh, covering the
   audit-persistence case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the
   tolerance).
2. A unit test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` is true for a
   just-persisted audit (auditedAt and updatedAt differ by milliseconds).
3. A unit test asserts a genuinely stale audit (item updated well after the
   audit) is still false (stale), unchanged.
4. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`
   continue to use the imported `isAuditFresh` as the sole filter; a
   just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
5. Both consumers import the same helper; no competing freshness comparison
   is introduced in the dispatch or icon paths.

## Notes / Open questions

- `isAuditFresh` currently hard-codes a magic `60000` ms literal. Prefer
  naming a constant (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`) and routing
  both consumers through it.
- Reconcile the comparison shape of `isAuditFresh` (`auditTime > updateTime -
  buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics from the SorraAgents fix so
  both projects express the same intent. Confirm the target semantics with the
  operator before implementing.

## References

- discovered-from: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents audit_runner child
  freshness at-or-near fix) — canonical reference implementation.
- related-to: WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (Audit candidate selection),
  WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R (Audit dispatch tier), parent WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG.
data.title: Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher

Mechanism under investigation: wl update --needs-producer-review bumps updatedAt (packages/shared/src/database.ts update()); herdr's isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt) (packages/herdr/src/icons.ts) then reports stale, which (a) degrades the TUI audit icon and (b) re-selects the item for audit-tier dispatch (selectAuditCandidate, packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts).

Every 30 seconds the herdr plugin should retrieve all in_progress work items and attempt to match an active pane to the work item. If none is found then set to either completed, blocked or open. This work item should be blocked on the one to add work item id to pane titles, which can then be used to match panes. All tabs in the current workspace should be searched.

# Write unit tests for auto-downgrade of critical priority

## Goal
Add comprehensive unit tests covering the auto-downgrade behavior for critical priority items transitioning to terminal states.

## Test Coverage Required

Per Acceptance Criteria 4 of parent (WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9):

1. **`wl update --status completed`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
2. **`wl update --stage in_review`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
3. **`wl close`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
4. **No-op: non-critical priorities** — verify high/medium/low unchanged on terminal transition
5. **No-op: non-terminal transitions** — verify critical priority unchanged when moving between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`)

## Implementation Notes

- Tests should use the existing test infrastructure (see `tests/database.test.ts` and `tests/cli/`)
- Follow the existing test patterns for `cascadePriorityDowngrade` tests
- Tests should verify both the priority change AND the reporting output (AC3 of parent)
- Consider both JSON and human-readable output paths

### Key Files
- `tests/database.test.ts` — database layer tests
- `tests/cli/` — CLI command tests (update, close)

## Goal

Amend the pane-title builders (WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y deliverable, landed in commit 66e4b8c8) so the work-item ID always survives the 60-char truncation and the prefixes become 'Downtime: ' / 'Manual: ' (dropping the word 'triggered'). This is a prerequisite for the hydrator (parent: Herdr hydrator: rescue in_progress work items with no active pane — WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI), which matches panes by the trailing ' - WL-<id>' in the title.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. buildManuallyTriggeredPaneTitle produces titles with prefix 'Manual: ' (e.g. 'Manual: implement <title> - WL-<id>'); no 'triggered' text anywhere in the output.
2. buildDowntimePaneTitle produces titles with prefix 'Downtime: ' (e.g. 'Downtime: implement <title> - WL-<id>'); no 'triggered' text.
3. For any title (incl. those exceeding MAX_PANE_TITLE_LENGTH=60), the truncated pane title always retains the full trailing ' - WL-<id>' suffix (truncation cuts the head/middle, never the ID tail).
4. Existing expectations updated: pane-title.test.ts behaviour tests, index.test.ts lines 98/104, and downtime-worker.ts doc comments (3 sites).
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts — builders + truncation
- packages/herdr/src/pane-title.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts (doc comments only)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Change prefixes: 'Manually triggered ' → 'Manual: ', 'Downtime triggered ' → 'Downtime: '.
2. Change truncation strategy: keep the trailing ' - WL-<id>' (and any spouse suffix) intact; truncate the head/middle when over MAX_PANE_TITLE_LENGTH.
3. Update pane-title.test.ts truncation tests (ID preservation) and prefix expectations.
4. Update index.test.ts expectations and downtime-worker.ts comment blocks.

# Intake Brief — Replace binary author-identity gate with configurable author whitelist (WL-0MTGDW58X007UJDS)

## Problem Statement

`wl sync` currently uses a binary author-identity gate (`syncAllowForeignAuthor` boolean): it either allows only commits from the local `user.email` or allows all foreign authors. This causes false-positive refusals for single operators with multiple emails/machines and does not scale for team or CI scenarios that need a selective allow-list.

## Users

- **Single operator, multiple machines/emails** — wants sync to succeed when their own secondary email appears on the remote without opening the gate to everyone.
- **Team lead / shared repo** — wants to allow a known set of collaborators' emails while still rejecting unknown authors.
- **CI / automation** — wants to allow a bot email in addition to the human operator without disabling the gate entirely.

### Example User Stories

- As a developer with `sorra@thewizardscode.com` on laptop and `alice@company.com` on CI, I want to whitelist both emails in `.worklog/worklog.yaml` so `wl sync` merges remote commits from either without requiring `--allow-foreign-author` on every run.
- As a project maintainer, I want the default (`syncAllowedAuthors: []`) to preserve the strictest behavior (only local `user.email`) so existing single-author repos see no security regression.
- As an operator who previously used `syncAllowForeignAuthor: true` or `--allow-foreign-author`, I want that flag to keep working (mapped to allow-all) so I am not broken by the migration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Config schema:** `syncAllowedAuthors` is accepted in `.worklog/config.yaml` / `config.defaults.yaml` with validation: `[]` (empty list, default), non-empty string list, `null`, or `true` (allow-all). Invalid types are rejected with a clear error.
- [ ] **AC2 — Gate behavior:** Empty list enforces current behavior (only local `user.email` accepted); non-empty list accepts any email in the whitelist; `null`/`true` allows any author (equivalent to current `--allow-foreign-author`). Empty-author commits are always refused regardless of whitelist.
- [ ] **AC3 — CLI compatibility:** `wl sync --allow-foreign-author` still works and overrides the config to allow-all for that invocation; help text (`wl sync --help`) explains the whitelist model (`[]` default, list, `null`/`true` allow-all) and the flag's override semantics. Existing `--allow-foreign-author` users are unaffected.
- [ ] **AC4 — Tests:** Automated tests cover: empty-list strict gating, non-empty whitelist allows listed / rejects unlisted, `null`/`true` allows all, empty-email always refused, and CLI flag override. Existing sync author-gate tests continue to pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Docs & suite:** Help text and relevant docs (e.g. `SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` / `CONFIG.md` or equivalent) describe the whitelist model. All related documentation and code comments are updated. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Default `[]` must preserve current security posture — no widening of the gate for existing repos without explicit config change.
- Empty author email is never bypassed (neither whitelist nor `--allow-foreign-author` nor `null`/`true` allows it).
- Backward compatibility: `syncAllowForeignAuthor` boolean and `--allow-foreign-author` flag must keep working; migration should not break existing users. Prefer whitelist as canonical, boolean as deprecated alias or mapped value.
- Email comparison should be case-insensitive (or documented as case-sensitive if intentionally strict) — assumption: case-insensitive, trimmed comparison.
- Minimal scope: config + gate logic + CLI flag wiring + help/docs + tests. No changes to merge logic beyond the gate.

## Existing State

- Author-identity gate lives in `src/sync.ts` (`checkAuthorIdentity`, `enforceAuthorIdentityGate`, `getConfiguredUserEmail`, `getRemoteAuthorCommits`) and is wired in `src/commands/sync.ts` via `getSyncDefaults` / `performSync` → `enforceAuthorIdentityGate`.
- Config key `syncAllowForeignAuthor?: boolean` is defined in `packages/shared/src/types.ts` and consumed in `src/commands/sync.ts` (`getSyncDefaults`). No `syncAllowedAuthors` exists yet.
- `src/config.ts` loads/merges `config.defaults.yaml` + `config.yaml` and validates statuses/stages; no whitelist validation.
- Related work: WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB (identity gate), WL-0MSUEO62N0019P3S (checkAuthorIdentity), WL-0MSUEOAQO0081TJH (wire gate + flag + sync-point), WL-0MTGH78A4000ZVNB (refusal verbosity/exit).

## Desired Change

- Add `syncAllowedAuthors?: string[] | null | true` to `WorklogConfig` (canonical whitelist). Keep `syncAllowForeignAuthor` as deprecated alias that maps to `null` (allow-all) when `syncAllowedAuthors` is unset, or document precedence.
- Add `syncAllowedAuthors: []` (or commented example) to `config.defaults.yaml` (test fixture defaults) and update validation in `src/config.ts` to accept `[]`, `string[]`, `null`, `true`.
- Replace binary gate in `src/sync.ts` (`checkAuthorIdentity` / `enforceAuthorIdentityGate`) to read the whitelist from config: `[]` → only `user.email`; non-empty → `user.email` plus listed emails; `null`/`true` → allow all (except empty-email).
- Update `src/commands/sync.ts` `getSyncDefaults` and CLI registration so `--allow-foreign-author` overrides to allow-all (and optionally `--sync-allowed-authors` or equivalent if desired; at minimum flag → allow-all). Update help text to explain whitelist model.
- Update docs (`SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` and/or `CONFIG.md` / `DATA_SYNCING.md`) and add tests covering AC4.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — Add `syncAllowedAuthors?: string[] | null | boolean` to `WorklogConfig`; keep `syncAllowForeignAuthor` as deprecated alias
- `src/config.ts` — Validate/normalize `syncAllowedAuthors` (allow `[]`, `string[]`, `null`, `true`); merge with defaults
- `src/sync.ts` — Modify `AuthorIdentityOptions` / `checkAuthorIdentity` / `enforceAuthorIdentityGate` to enforce whitelist instead of pure boolean
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — Wire `syncAllowedAuthors` via `getSyncDefaults`; keep `--allow-foreign-author` as allow-all override; update help text
- `src/sync-defaults.ts` / `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` (test fixture) — Add default `syncAllowedAuthors: []` and/or documentation
- `docs/sync/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md` (or `CONFIG.md` / `DATA_SYNCING.md`) — Document whitelist model
- `tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts` / `tests/cli/sync-author-gate.test.ts` — Add whitelist coverage

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB** — Sync: identity gate — refuse merge of foreign/empty-author commits (completed) — parent feature this refines
- **WL-0MSUEO62N0019P3S** — Implement checkAuthorIdentity gate in src/sync.ts (completed)
- **WL-0MSUEOAQO0081TJH** — Wire identity gate into wl sync + config flag + sync-point persistence (completed)
- **WL-0MTGH78A4000ZVNB** — Author-identity gate refusal must surface at default verbosity and exit non-zero (completed)
- **WL-0MTGH7ALW002BOQN** — Recovery path for already-diverged worklog repos (completed)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk — Ambiguous precedence:** Both `syncAllowForeignAuthor` and `syncAllowedAuthors` could be set. Mitigation: define clear precedence (whitelist wins when set; boolean is deprecated alias / maps to `null` only when whitelist absent); document and test.
- **Risk — Email normalization:** Case/whitespace differences could cause false refusals. Mitigation: trim + case-insensitive comparison; document.
- **Risk — Scope creep:** Temptation to add regex/wildcard matching or per-branch whitelists. Mitigation: out of scope; record as follow-up work items if requested.
- **Assumption — `null` and `true` are equivalent allow-all** per proposed solution; `undefined`/absent means default `[]`.
- **Assumption — Empty-email gate remains unconditional** (never bypassed).
- **Assumption — No new CLI flag for the list needed in v1**; whitelist is config-only, CLI flag remains allow-all override. A `--sync-allowed-authors` flag can be a follow-up.

## Appendix — Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should `syncAllowForeignAuthor: true` be deprecated or kept indefinitely?" — Answer: Keep for backward compatibility; treat as alias that maps to `syncAllowedAuthors: null` when whitelist is unset. Precedence: explicit `syncAllowedAuthors` wins. Source: Proposed solution AC + existing-state analysis; no producer input yet — recorded as assumption.
- Q: "Should email comparison be case-insensitive?" — Answer: Assumed case-insensitive trimmed comparison (common for emails). Alternative (case-sensitive) would cause surprising refusals; document choice. Source: assumption, to be confirmed if producer prefers strict matching.
- Q: "Is a CLI flag to set the whitelist needed (e.g. `--sync-allowed-authors a@x,b@y`)?" — Answer: Not required for v1; whitelist is config-only, `--allow-foreign-author` covers the allow-all escape hatch. CLI list flag can be a follow-up if requested. Source: scope constraint, inferred from proposed solution.

## Related Docs

- `src/sync.ts`
- `src/commands/sync.ts`
- `src/config.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/types.ts`
- `src/sync-defaults.ts`
- `docs/sync/SYNC_IDENTITY_GATE.md`
- `tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts`

Potentially related docs: `CONFIG.md`, `DATA_SYNCING.md`

## Summary
Remove time-based expiry of coordination entries so offers persist until dispatched or found stale via eligibility check (AC1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `pruneStaleEntries` call removed from `dispatchFromCoordination` — no dispatch cycle removes entries by wall-clock age
- [ ] No coordination entry removed solely by `lastUpdated` age; machine file `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` (and legacy per-worklog files if read) follow same rule
- [ ] Leadership lease (`leader-election.ts:DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS=300`) unchanged — only coordination entry TTL removed
- [ ] Existing prune tests inverted/removed: entries older than 5 min remain present after a dispatch cycle when still dispatchable
- [ ] Fail-safe preserved: missing/corrupt coordination or lease files degrade to no dispatch this cycle, never crash

## Minimal Implementation
- Neutralize/remove `pruneStaleEntries` for the machine coordination file (`packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts`) — keep export as no-op/deprecated if needed for compat, update header comment
- Remove `pruneStaleEntries` invocation + pruneCount log + re-read-after-prune block in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchFromCoordination`
- Do not touch scoring/rank reuse (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2); keep zero npm deps for fetcher path if touched

## Dependencies
- None

## Deliverables
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts` (prune tests inverted)

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts`
